newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus voters face seven questions.
newsitem.headline: Belarus voters face seven questions.

text.p: Belarussian voters are facing a baffling list of seven referendum questions on Sunday, the first four proposed by President Alexander Lukashenko and a further three by parliament.
Lukashenko said on Saturday the result of the referendum would be binding.

1. Asks Belarussians if the national holiday should be moved from July 27 -- the day the republic's first ever constitution was passed in 1991 -- to July 3 to commemorate the day in 1944 when Belarus was liberated by Soviet forces from Adolf Hitler's Nazi troops.

2. Proposes Lukashenko's new edition of the draft constitution. It would allow him to restart his five-year term from the day of the vote, to appoint half the constitutional court and electoral commission and to create a new upper house of parliament with 60 senators, including six appointed by him, and reduce the number of seats in the lower house to 110.
3. Asks "Do you support the free, unlimited buying and selling of land?" (Lukashenko is against.)
4. Asks if the death penalty should be abolished, a move which Lukashenko also opposes.
5. Proposes the deputies' constitutional draft, which would abolish the presidency and award more powers to a cabinet led by a prime minister who would have most power.
6. Proposes direct elections of local leaders who are currently appointed by Lukashenko.
7. Seeks approval for open funding to state institutions to come directly from budget. Lukashenko has a non-budget fund controlled by him to which parliament has no access.
